utility.notes: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power Company, operating as Black Hills Energy, is the established dominant electric utility serving Cheyenne and southeastern Wyoming, filing its own tariffs (including Wyoming P.S.C. Tariff No. 13 governing net metering) with the Wyoming Public Service Commission. The utility's own consumer-facing website (blackhillsenergy.com) was unreachable this session (DNS resolution failure and connection resets across three independent WebFetch attempts, plus two denied browser navigation attempts), so this record relies on Wyoming state government sources for the applicable net metering law rather than the utility's own program materials.

interconnection_url.notes: Wyoming does not leave net metering to individual utility discretion — it is a mandatory statewide law (Wyoming Statutes Title 37, Chapter 16, Article 1, Sections 37-16-101 through 103) applicable to all Wyoming investor-owned electric utilities and electric cooperatives, confirmed by directly reading the current (2025) statute text via Justia's official-code mirror. A 2024 bill (HB0094) that would have raised the net metering capacity cap from 25 kW to 750 kW for customer-generators died in the Wyoming Legislature without passing; the Wyoming Legislative Service Office's own 2019 research memorandum independently confirms the same 25 kW cap and annual-reset compensation structure described in the statute. value.program_or_pathway: Net metering under Wyoming Statutes Title 37, Chapter 16, Article 1 (Sections 37-16-101 through 103) — a mandatory statewide net metering law applicable to all Wyoming investor-owned electric utilities and electric cooperatives, including Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power Company d/b/a Black Hills Energy.
other_conditions: Eligible net metering systems must use solar, wind, biomass, or hydropower, be located on the customer-generator's own premises, and be sized primarily to offset the customer-generator's own electricity requirements (W.S. 37-16-101).

Excess generation is credited at the full retail rate on the customer's bill for the following month, and unused monthly credits carry forward within the year — but at the start of each calendar year, any remaining unused kilowatt-hour credit balance from the prior year is sold to the utility at its own PSC-filed avoided-cost rate rather than carried forward indefinitely (W.S. 37-16-103).

The electric utility must offer a bidirectional energy meter to each eligible net-metered customer-generator and may not charge that customer a minimum monthly charge greater than other customers in the same rate class (W.S. 37-16-102).

A 2024 bill (HB0094) that would have raised the net metering capacity cap from 25 kW to 750 kW for customer-generators died in the Wyoming Legislature and did not become law; the 25 kW cap remains in effect as of this session.

permit_fees.notes: The City of Cheyenne's own Building Permit Information page states that permit fees are based on total project valuation (materials plus labor), with a separate plan review fee equal to 65% of the permit fee, but does not publish a fixed dollar figure or a fee-schedule table on the page itself — left null rather than guessed. No Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power Company interconnection application fee was found this session; the utility's own program materials were unreachable (see utility field notes).

rebates.notes: No rebate or incentive dollar amount was independently confirmed from a primary source this session for Cheyenne or Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power Company specifically.
